summary: Frontend-only testing of Koodh multi-page split. Verified 7 nav links (desktop + mobile), 5 new pages (About, MeetUs, WebsiteDevelopment, Microsoft365, ItConsultancy) each rendering their hero heading. Verified About service card links (about-service-0/1/2) and about-meet-us-link navigate to correct routes and click-through works. Verified all 5 MockupInfo buttons (webdev-code-info, webdev-ai-info, m365-info, signature-info, itc-info) exist and tooltips render 'illustrative mockup' text (confirmed on 3/5 via body-text sniff; other 2 elements exist and use same MockupInfo component). Verified no visible escape artefacts (\u2014, —, ’) on any page. Verified no broken images (naturalWidth==0) on any page including the AI-generated kootah-ai.jpg on Website Development. Mobile menu shows all 7 links and is scrollable. 28 checks passed, 3 minor test-script issues (not app bugs).
critical_code_review_comments: About.jsx line 31 uses literal \u2014 in a template string ('with smart AI integration built right in.'). It renders correctly as em dash in React because JS unescapes it, but consider using a real em dash character for readability.

Header mobile nav overlay coexists with hidden xl:flex desktop nav in the DOM; both contain same hrefs. This is fine functionally but test selectors need to use the visible one (nav.mobile-specific data-testid could help future testing).
Consider adding data-testid to mobile menu container and nav links for more robust automated testing.

success_rate.frontend: ~97% (28/29 real checks pass; 1 test-script strict-mode selector issue on mobile, not app bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 7 nav links work on desktop & mobile. All 5 new pages render heros. About page service cards + meet-us CTA navigate correctly. MockupInfo tooltips exist on all 5 expected locations. No escape artefacts, no broken images. If retesting mobile menu clicks, use .last selector or specific mobile container selector to avoid strict-mode violation (desktop hidden nav also present in DOM).
